title: Every stage skill carries its purpose, method, next activity, delegations and boundaries from the canonical definition
statement: Each canonical stage definition in `stages/*.json` declares its purpose, its method, its rules for selecting the next question or activity, its allowed delegations with the capabilities each requires, its mutation boundary, its approval boundary and its expected completion summary, and each generated `kiln-stage-<stage-id>` skill carries those seven from its definition. None of them is supplied by the generator's templates or inferred from another field - in particular a stage's purpose is not taken from `producesProse`, which describes its outputs. The generator refuses a definition that lacks a required field rather than filling it in, and the check fails, naming the skill, when any generated field no longer matches its definition.
notes: ⚠️ DEFERRED FROM TSK-0046 ON PURPOSE (O1 and F88, 2026-09-13). TSK-0046 promised these seven, and no canonical definition carries any of them: `stages/*.json` has a name, a decision owner, outputs and exit criteria, and nothing else. A generator asked to emit them would have to write them into its own templates or borrow another field, which recreates exactly the drift CMP-0033 exists to prevent - two descriptions of one pipeline, each invisible from the other. So the definitions gain the fields first, and generation follows. ⚠️ PURPOSE WAS NEARLY BORROWED (F88). The first generator printed `producesProse` under Purpose. That field describes outputs; relabelling it is inference by another route, and it is refused for the same reason a template default is. ⚠️ A TEMPLATE DEFAULT IS A FAILURE, NOT A CONVENIENCE. A skill that says 'delegate as appropriate' because its definition was silent reads exactly like one whose definition said so; refusing the definition is the only way the gap stays visible. ⚠️ DELEGATIONS AND BOUNDARIES NAME ROLES, NOT RULES. Allowed delegations and the mutation boundary refer to the roles and write boundaries `lib/specialists/contract.mjs` and TSK-0051's roster define, rather than restating them per stage, which is why this depends on TSK-0051.
